chapterTitle: FBISE Annual Board Examination Section A Simulator 1
subject: english

questions.question: 'Sweet scented stuff' is an example of which type of imagery?
questions.explanation: Olfactory imagery engages the sense of smell. 'Sweet scented' directly evokes the sensation of smell.

questions.question: 'All the best singers will be awarded prizes.' The underlined part 'All the best singers' contains a/an:
questions.explanation: 'All the best singers' consists of a determiner ('All'), an article and adjective ('the best'), and a head noun ('singers'), together functioning as a subject noun phrase.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is an optative sentence?

options.A: You should take care of your parents.

questions.explanation: An optative sentence expresses a wish, prayer, or benediction, typically initiated with the modal auxiliary 'May'.

questions.question: 'The melted chocolate is out of shape.' The underlined word 'melted' is a/an:
questions.explanation: 'Melted' is the past participle form of the verb 'melt' used as a participial adjective to describe the noun 'chocolate'.

questions.question: An expression so often used that its originality and effectiveness has been lost is known as a/an:
questions.explanation: A cliché is a trite, stereotyped expression or phrase that has become commonplace through overuse.

questions.question: Choose the correctly structured conditional sentence:

options.A: If I had time, I would have recheck my paper.
options.B: If I had had time, I would have rechecked my paper.
options.C: If I had time, I would rechecked my paper.
options.D: If I have time, I would rechecked my paper.

questions.explanation: Third conditional structures follow: If + Past Perfect ('had had'), would have + past participle ('would have rechecked').

questions.question: Which sentence has the use of a Prepositional phrase?

options.A: By the light of the moon, everything was very charming.

questions.explanation: 'By the light of the moon' is a prepositional phrase showing circumstantial time and location.

questions.question: 'We must learn to live together as brothers or perish together as fools.' is an example of:
questions.explanation: Antithesis emphasizes the contrast between two diametrically opposed ideas ('live together as brothers' vs 'perish together as fools') in parallel syntax.

questions.question: Which sentence has the use of a gerund phrase?

options.B: Eating small meals throughout the day can help you avoid hunger pains.
options.C: Writing is more difficult than typing.

questions.explanation: 'Eating small meals throughout the day' consists of a gerund ('Eating') with its object and prepositional modifier, functioning as the subject of the clause.

questions.question: The chief guest gave ___ the prizes. Choose the correct phrasal verb:
questions.explanation: 'Give away' is the formal phrasal verb meaning to distribute honors, awards, or certificates during ceremonies.

questions.question: Jennifer hears a smoke alarm next door and smells burnt bread. We can infer that:
questions.explanation: Auditory evidence (smoke alarm next door) coupled with olfactory evidence (burnt bread) logically supports the deduction that the neighbor burnt breakfast.

questions.question: 'Seething with intense desire to annihilate the belligerent enemy.' The word 'annihilate' means:
questions.explanation: 'Annihilate' is derived from Latin nihil ('nothing'), signifying total obliteration or complete destruction.

questions.question: 'Let's go for a walk.' The underlined verb 'go' functions as a/an:
questions.explanation: After causative verbs and imperatives like 'let', the infinitive appears without the particle 'to', known as a bare infinitive.

questions.question: Which one of the following sentences exemplifies the use of irony?

options.B: My mom has a heart of gold.
options.C: Oh great! Now you have broken my new glasses.
options.D: My love is like a red rose.

questions.explanation: Verbal irony expresses a meaning that is the opposite of the literal words spoken ('Oh great!' used when property is ruined).

questions.question: An essay that analyses characters, themes, setting, and conflict of a drama or novel is called a/an:
questions.explanation: A literary essay formally deconstructs aesthetic, thematic, and structural devices within a published literary work.

questions.question: 'The man who was hunting deer escaped narrowly from dropping into the water.' The clause 'who was hunting deer' is a/an:
questions.explanation: 'Who was hunting deer' is an adjective (relative) clause that qualifies the noun antecedent 'The man'.

questions.question: Which sentence has the correct sequence of tenses?

options.A: He planned that he will visit Pakistan soon.
options.B: He has planned that he would visit Pakistan soon.
options.C: He planned that he would visit Pakistan soon.
options.D: He had planned that he will visit Pakistan soon.

questions.explanation: When the principal clause verb is in the past tense ('planned'), subordinate verbs shift to past modal forms ('would visit').

questions.question: Which of the following sentences has the use of a linking verb?

options.A: The boys were playing a cricket match.

questions.explanation: In 'My cousin is a teacher', the verb 'is' serves as a copula (linking verb) connecting the subject to its predicate noun complement without describing an action.

questions.question: When the narrator knows every character's private thoughts, feelings, and secret motivations, the story is told in:
questions.explanation: Third-person omniscient narration provides all-knowing, godlike awareness across all characters simultaneously.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences has the use of a ditransitive verb?

options.C: Sara sent a package to Azan.

questions.explanation: A ditransitive verb governs two objects: a direct object ('a package') and an indirect object/recipient ('Azan').
